name: MarineCadastre AIS vessel traffic (US waters)
publisher: NOAA Office for Coastal Management and BOEM (MarineCadastre.gov)
licence: Generally considered public domain (per MarineCadastre AIS FAQ); provided for coastal and ocean planning, not for regulatory or enforcement use
format: Daily ZIP files of CSV (2015 onward); File Geodatabase before 2015
coverage: US EEZ, Great Lakes and Guam, 2009 onward; Alaska data ended 2021-03-29
why_useful: Train vessel-track, anomaly and AIS-gap detection models on real ship positions, including Alaskan Arctic waters up to early 2021.
notes: RESTRICTED USE: the FAQ limits use to coastal and ocean planning, not regulatory or enforcement purposes. Derived from US Coast Guard NAIS; positions down-sampled to 1 minute. 2024 alone is 366 daily files totalling 116.7 GB, so take a few days. Bulk index: coast.noaa.gov/htdata/CMSP/AISDataHandler/

name: Norwegian open AIS feed (incl. Svalbard and Jan Mayen)
licence: Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD)
format: Live raw AIS (NMEA) over TCP; BarentsWatch API and map services
coverage: Norwegian economic zone plus protection zones off Svalbard and Jan Mayen; live
why_useful: Stream live High Arctic ship positions into a dashboard or dark-vessel alert prototype without signing up.
notes: Open stream at IP 153.44.253.27 port 5631 (per Kystverket). Fishing vessels under 15 m and leisure craft under 45 m are excluded from open data. Historical data needs an application to post@kystverket.no.

name: Global Fishing Watch APIs (AIS activity and SAR vessel detections)
licence: CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial; contact Global Fishing Watch for commercial use)
format: REST APIs (JSON); bulk downloads for registered users
coverage: Global incl. Canadian waters; AIS-based vessel activity plus satellite radar (SAR) vessel and offshore infrastructure detections
why_useful: Compare radar-detected vessels with AIS broadcasts to flag possible dark vessels, loitering or encounters.
notes: NON-COMMERCIAL: CC BY-NC 4.0; startups need permission from Global Fishing Watch for commercial use. Register, request an API token, agree to terms and credit Global Fishing Watch. APIs cover vessel identity, fishing events, encounters, loitering, port visits, AIS presence and SAR detections.

name: Global Shipping Traffic Density
publisher: World Bank (with IMF World Seaborne Trade Monitoring System)
format: Raster density grids in 6 ZIP files (20.5 MB to 510.1 MB)
coverage: Global, Jan 2015 to Feb 2021, 0.005 degree (~500 m) cells; layers by vessel type
why_useful: Use as a baseline of normal shipping lanes to spot unusual Arctic routes or score how busy an area is.
notes: Built from hourly AIS positions. Separate layers for commercial, fishing, oil and gas, passenger, leisure and all vessels.

name: Arctic Ship Traffic Data (ASTD)
publisher: PAME (Protection of the Arctic Marine Environment), Arctic Council
licence: Governed by the Cooperative Agreement among the Arctic States Regarding Arctic Ship Traffic Data Sharing; access by approved application
format: Online system (map.astd.is) with data download for approved users
coverage: Arctic (PAME-defined area); ship tracks by type, 400+ ports and communities, ship emissions; online maps show 2013-2025
why_useful: Analyse years of Arctic ship traffic by vessel type and port to decide where monitoring sensors matter most.
notes: REQUEST ONLY: email the application form to pame@pame.is. Eligible: Arctic State agencies, Arctic Council observers, students and media (limited free access), not-for-profit research groups. Commercial firms are not listed. Approval is by review, so apply before the event.

name: RADARSAT-1 SAR image archive
publisher: Canadian Space Agency / Natural Resources Canada
format: GeoTIFF; Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF on AWS (s3://radarsat-r1-l1-cog, ca-central-1)
coverage: Historical archive from Canada's RADARSAT-1 (launched November 1995)
why_useful: Practise SAR ship and sea-ice detection on Canadian radar imagery that loads straight from a public cloud bucket.
notes: AWS access needs no account (aws s3 ls --no-sign-request s3://radarsat-r1-l1-cog/). Also via EODMS (account). AWS registry notes an NRCan public processing service for the raw archive since 2025-12-18.

name: RADARSAT Constellation Mission (RCM) public image products
licence: RCM Public User License Agreement (royalty-free, commercial use allowed; the RCM imagery itself may not be sold; credit 'RADARSAT Constellation Mission Imagery © Government of Canada (year)')
format: SAR image products via EODMS
coverage: Public products: 100 m over world maritime areas; 16 m or coarser over Canada's landmass (latitude limits apply)
why_useful: Pull Canadian SAR scenes over ocean and sea ice for wide-area maritime and ice monitoring demos.
notes: RESTRICTED: the RCM imagery may not be sold and two attribution lines are mandatory. Register a free EODMS account to become a public user; finer products need vetted-user security screening.

name: OSSDD - OpenSARShip Ship Detection Dataset (Sentinel-1)
licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (annotations, metadata, code); Sentinel-1 imagery under Copernicus terms
format: 32-bit GeoTIFF chips (VV and VH), binary masks, axis-aligned and rotated boxes; ZIP or WebDataset shards; 72.3 GB
coverage: 15,197 Sentinel-1 GRD patches with 55,759 annotated ships
why_useful: Train a ship detector on the same free Sentinel-1 radar that covers the Canadian Arctic, then run it on new scenes.
notes: NON-COMMERCIAL: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (share-alike). Not gated. Described in arXiv 2608.01963.

name: HRSID - High-Resolution SAR Images Dataset
format: JPG or PNG image chips with COCO-style annotations; Google Drive and Baidu links
coverage: 5,604 high-resolution SAR images (0.5 m, 1 m, 3 m) with 16,951 ship instances
why_useful: Benchmark ship detection and segmentation on high-resolution radar, including crowded inshore scenes.
notes: COPYLEFT: GPL-3.0 as published in the repo; check fit before using in a commercial product. Offshore/inshore splits and negative samples are offered.

name: Canadian Ice Service ice charts
publisher: Environment and Climate Change Canada - Canadian Ice Service
format: Vector ice charts (Egg Code) via the MSC Datamart; archive charts in GIF and E00
coverage: Canadian waters; daily, image-analysis and regional charts 2014 to present; archive back to 1968
why_useful: Overlay official sea-ice conditions on ship tracks to judge which Arctic routes are passable and where risk is rising.
notes: Archive record (OGL): iceweb1.cis.ec.gc.ca/Archive20/. Analysis-ready SIGRID-3 shapefiles from 2006 are also distributed by NSIDC (G02171; version 2 now available).

name: Sea Ice Index, Version 4 (G02135)
publisher: NOAA@NSIDC (National Snow and Ice Data Center)
licence: No licence named; NSIDC requires citing the dataset (DOI 10.7265/a98x-0f50)
format: CSV, GeoTIFF, shapefile, PNG
coverage: Arctic and Antarctic, daily and monthly, 1978-10-26 to present, 25 km grid
why_useful: Chart daily Arctic ice extent and concentration as a context layer or for simple seasonal access forecasts.
notes: Direct HTTPS download at noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/ (no login noted). NSIDC has reduced this product to a Basic level of service.

name: Marine Regions maritime boundaries (World EEZ v12 and related layers)
format: Shapefile, GeoPackage, KML, GeoJSON
coverage: Global EEZs, territorial seas, contiguous zones, internal waters, high seas, IHO sea areas; World EEZ v12 dated 2023-10-25 (122 MB)
why_useful: Check whether a vessel is inside Canada's EEZ or territorial sea and alert when a track crosses a boundary.
notes: RESTRICTED PURPOSE: the disclaimer says Marine Regions is for scientific, educational and research purposes, not legal, resource-exploration or navigational use. Cite 'Flanders Marine Institute (2026): MarineRegions.org'.

name: Canadian Protected and Conserved Areas Database (CPCAD)
format: File Geodatabase; ESRI REST and WMS services
coverage: Canada; marine and terrestrial protected areas, OECMs and recognised Indigenous protected and conserved areas; updated annually
why_useful: Flag vessels loitering or fishing inside marine protected areas as higher-priority alerts.
notes: Compiled with federal, provincial and territorial reporting authorities.

name: GEBCO_2026 global bathymetry grid (with IBCAO Arctic grid)
publisher: GEBCO (General Bathymetric Chart of the Oceans)
licence: Public domain (GEBCO Grid 'placed in the public domain and may be used free of charge')
format: netCDF, GeoTIFF, Esri ASCII; download app for custom areas; OPeNDAP
coverage: Global 15 arc-second grid; IBCAO v5.2 Arctic grid (June 2026) at 100, 200 and 400 m
why_useful: Add water depth to route and risk models, for example where deep-draft ships cannot go in Arctic channels.
notes: NOT FOR NAVIGATION. IBCAO v5.2 (GeoTIFF, 1 GB to 25.2 GB) is on gebco.net/data-products/gridded-bathymetry-data/arctic-ocean with its own disclaimer and no formal open licence stated.

name: OpenSky Network ADS-B data (REST API and historical database)
licence: OpenSky General Terms of Use & Data License Agreement; free full access for research, aviation authorities, government and non-profits; commercial entities must obtain a licence
format: REST API (JSON state vectors); Trino SQL for history; datasets incl. aircraft database and weekly 24 h state vector samples
coverage: Global crowdsourced ADS-B and Mode S; live and historical
why_useful: Build a live airspace picture or flag aircraft behaving oddly near a protected site using real flight positions.
notes: NON-COMMERCIAL BY DEFAULT: commercial entities must obtain a licence. Anonymous REST use gets only the latest state vectors at 10 s resolution and 400 credits/day; OAuth2 client accounts get more. Historical (Trino) access is by application.

name: adsb.lol globe history (daily ADS-B traces)
licence: ODbL 1.0 (repository also lists a CC0 licence file)
format: Daily GitHub releases of split tar archives with gzip JSON (readsb traces and heatmaps)
coverage: Global community ADS-B feeder network; per-year repositories (2026 shown)
why_useful: Replay whole days of aircraft tracks to test tracking code; NIC/NACp fields can be mapped to show GNSS interference.
notes: SHARE-ALIKE: ODbL requires public derived databases to stay under ODbL. Join split parts before extracting (cat part.aa part.ab | tar -xf -). Trace entries can include nic, nac_p, sil and gpsOkBefore (readsb JSON docs). Whole repo is about 1,762 GiB, so fetch single days.

name: OurAirports open airport data
format: CSV: airports (12.7 MB), runways, navaids, airport frequencies, comments, countries, regions
coverage: Worldwide incl. Canada; updated nightly
why_useful: Map aerodromes, runways and navaids to define protected zones around airports for drone alerts.
notes: Comes with no guarantee of accuracy or fitness for use; not an official aeronautical source.

name: openAIP aeronautical database
licence: CC BY-NC 4.0 (openAIP allows its data inside paid apps but not selling the data itself)
format: Web exports and REST API
coverage: Worldwide airspaces, airports, navaids, obstacles, reporting points; community-maintained
why_useful: Draw controlled and restricted airspace polygons to check whether a detected drone is somewhere it should not be.
notes: NON-COMMERCIAL: CC BY-NC 4.0 (see openAIP clause on paid apps). Community data: check Canadian airspace completeness against official NAV CANADA publications before relying on it.

name: TrajAir general aviation trajectory dataset
format: Text files: frame, aircraft ID, x/y/z in km, wind x/y in m/s, at 1 Hz
coverage: Pittsburgh-Butler Regional Airport (KBTP), USA; Sep 2020 to Apr 2021, 111 days
why_useful: Train trajectory-prediction models that forecast where nearby aircraft will be, a core piece of airspace deconfliction.
notes: Download via KiltHub DOI 10.1184/R1/14866251. Collected with an ADS-B receiver (1090 and 978 MHz) plus METAR weather.

name: DroneRF dataset
format: CSV raw RF time-domain samples; over 40 GB
coverage: 227 segments: Parrot Bebop, Parrot AR.Drone 2.0, DJI Phantom 3 and background RF, 2.4 GHz band
why_useful: Train a classifier that detects drones and identifies model and flight mode from their radio signals.
notes: Licence confirmed from DataCite metadata for DOI 10.17632/f4c2b4n755.1. Described in Data in Brief (2019).

name: RFUAV drone RF benchmark
format: Raw IQ, spectrogram images, videos; Parquet conversion on Hugging Face
coverage: 37 UAV models; 100 MHz sampling rate (per project repo)
why_useful: Build and test RF drone identification across many commercial models from spectrograms or raw IQ.
notes: Hugging Face lists about 299 GB and the paper cites about 1.3 TB of raw data, so download a subset. Not gated. Code: github.com/kitoweeknd/RFUAV (Apache-2.0).

name: DeepSig RadioML datasets
format: HDF5 (RadioML 2018.01A); Python pickle (2016.10A, 2016.04C)
coverage: Synthetic IQ; 2018.01A has 24 modulation types and 2 million examples of 1,024 samples
why_useful: Prototype RF signal classifiers quickly before moving to real drone or jammer recordings.
notes: NON-COMMERCIAL: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. DeepSig calls these historical datasets with known errata and recommends real data for serious work.

name: Drone Detection Dataset (IR, visible video and audio)
format: Videos (IR and visible) with MATLAB .mat labels; audio clips; description spreadsheet
coverage: 650 videos (365 IR, 285 visible) with drone, bird, airplane and helicopter classes; 90 audio clips
why_useful: Train camera and thermal detectors that tell drones from birds and aircraft, plus a simple audio detector.
notes: About 203,328 annotated frames when extracted. Labels readable in Python via mcos-decoder. Repo cites Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.5500576.

name: Anti-UAV tracking datasets (Anti-UAV300, 410, 600)
format: Full HD video sequences with dense bounding-box annotations
coverage: Anti-UAV300: RGB and thermal IR; Anti-UAV410 and 600: thermal IR only
why_useful: Train and score trackers that keep a lock on small drones in thermal video against cluttered backgrounds.
notes: Download links (Google Drive, Baidu, ModelScope) are in the README.

name: DDL drone sound dataset (detection and localization)
format: Audio archives: real recordings 12.6 GB and synthesized 4.6 GB (17.3 GB total)
coverage: DJI Mini 2 and DJI Phantom 4 Pro plus no-drone recordings, labelled with bearing, range and altitude
why_useful: Build a microphone-array drone detector that also estimates direction and distance.
notes: File names encode timestamp, drone model, bearing, range, altitude, temperature and real vs synthesized.

name: Drone-vs-Bird Detection Challenge dataset
licence: Research use under a signed data usage agreement
format: Videos with per-frame text annotations
coverage: Videos of drones, often with birds, recorded at distance; grows with each challenge edition
why_useful: Benchmark camera-based detectors on the hard case of telling small distant drones from birds.
notes: REQUEST ONLY, RESEARCH USE: email wosdetc@googlegroups.com and sign the data usage agreement; allow lead time before the event.

name: Jammertest 2025 GNSS Interference Dataset
format: HDF5 (raw 8-bit IQ plus labels), split .h5.part files via Git LFS; about 299 MB
coverage: Jammertest 2025, Andøya, Norway; GNSS E1 and E5a; CW, sweep, PRN jamming, meaconing, spoofing, multi-source
why_useful: Train and test a jamming and spoofing classifier on labelled real-world interference recordings that fit on a laptop.
notes: NON-COMMERCIAL: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Zenodo holds pointers and docs; clone the linked GitHub repo and run git lfs pull. Two receivers: Innosense compact (81 MHz) and a CRPA array (100 MHz).

name: GNSS Jamming Response Dataset (L1 - 2025)
publisher: University of Ljubljana, Faculty of Electrical Engineering
format: Single JSON file (5.9 GB)
coverage: Three low-cost receivers (Ai-Thinker GP-01, u-blox NEO-6M, u-blox MAX-M10) under three jamming conditions at varying strengths
why_useful: Learn what jamming looks like in ordinary receiver outputs so a cheap device can warn that it is being jammed.
notes: File: jamming_dataset_august_2024.json. Companion paper: Electronics 2025, 14(9), 1797.

name: TEXBAT - Texas Spoofing Test Battery
publisher: University of Texas at Austin, Radionavigation Laboratory
licence: Custom: free to use, copy and modify for research purposes; users asked not to redistribute
format: Raw IF sample recordings (.bin)
coverage: Recorded GPS spoofing scenarios: TEXBAT 1.0 sets plus ds7 and ds8
why_useful: Test spoofing detectors against the standard benchmark of recorded GPS spoofing attacks.
notes: RESEARCH ONLY: no redistribution; get permission for commercial work. Cite Humphreys et al., ION GNSS 2012. Files are large raw recordings.

name: Tuni2025 GNSS spoofing dataset (Galileo E1 raw IQ)
format: Raw IQ .bin (interleaved 32-bit float), about 30 GB per scenario; PDF readme
coverage: 8 scenarios: 4 clear-sky and 4 with 1 to 5 spoofers; USRP-2945R at 50 MSps; spoofing from a Spectracom GSG-6
why_useful: Develop software-receiver spoofing detection on Galileo signals under a licence that allows commercial use.
notes: Download one scenario to keep size manageable.

name: Multi-Sensor Dataset From Android Smart Devices (raw GNSS)
format: ZIP (670.5 MB)
coverage: Raw GNSS measurements and other sensor data from several Android devices (file Android_GNSS_Dataset_Hervanta.zip)
why_useful: Experiment with phone-based positioning and integrity checks using raw measurements from ordinary Android phones.
notes: Logged with the authors' Mimir Android app.

name: IGS precise orbits, clocks and ionosphere maps
publisher: International GNSS Service (archived at NASA CDDIS and other data centres)
licence: IGS Data and Product Disclaimer and Terms of Use: free for scientific, educational and commercial users; attribution required
format: SP3 orbits, CLK clocks, ERP, IONEX ionosphere maps, SINEX
coverage: Global; ultra-rapid (4 times daily), rapid (~17 h latency), final (~13 days)
why_useful: Compute precise satellite positions and clocks to check whether a receiver's measurements are consistent or spoofed.
notes: NASA CDDIS (cddis.nasa.gov/archive/gnss/products) needs a free Earthdata Login; IGN and BKG mirrors are also listed. Not for life-critical use.

name: NRCan CSRS-PPP service and Canadian Active Control System GNSS data
publisher: Natural Resources Canada - Canadian Geodetic Survey
format: Upload RINEX; returns PDF report, .sum, .pos, .clk, .tro, CSV; CACS station RINEX downloads
coverage: Global PPP processing (GPS, GLONASS, Galileo); Canadian reference station network
why_useful: Get centimetre-level reference positions for your own GNSS logs, a baseline for measuring jamming or spoofing effects.
notes: Free service; sign-in account required. Ambiguity resolution for data after 2018-01-01; Galileo for data after 2022-11-27. CACS data, orbits and clocks: webapp.csrs-scrs.nrcan-rncan.gc.ca/geod/data-donnees/cacs-scca.php

name: NOAA SWPC space weather data services
format: JSON, text and netCDF feeds
coverage: Global; real-time planetary K-index, solar wind, GOES X-ray flux, alerts and forecasts
why_useful: Pull live geomagnetic and solar storm indicators to explain or predict GNSS degradation in a PNT dashboard.
notes: Product catalogue at spaceweather.gov/products-and-data; history via NCEI. Do not imply NOAA endorsement.

name: NRCan Geomagnetism Canada observatory data
licence: Custom NRCan terms: for your project only, not for sale or redistribution without written permission, not for commercial purposes; acknowledge NRCan
format: Minute and second observatory data via FDSN web service; Canadian magnetic indices
coverage: Canadian magnetic observatories (CANMOS), 1992 onward
why_useful: Detect geomagnetic storms over northern Canada that degrade GNSS accuracy and HF radio.
notes: NON-COMMERCIAL: commercial users need NRCan permission; no redistribution without written permission. Data before 1992 have known quality issues.

name: CHAIN - Canadian High Arctic Ionospheric Network
licence: Open access under the CHAIN Data Policy (per Government of Canada data policy)
format: GNSS TEC and scintillation receiver data; ionosonde data
coverage: About 24 stations across the Canadian Arctic, mostly in Nunavut
why_useful: Study how Arctic ionospheric disturbances degrade GNSS accuracy, a key PNT risk for northern operations.
notes: Open access, existing login or free registration. The server was intermittently unreachable during checks. Station and instrument counts come from public network descriptions; follow the CHAIN Data Policy when publishing.

name: World Magnetic Model 2025 (WMM2025)
format: Coefficient file (WMM.COF), C software, online calculators, contour maps (PDF, shapefile)
coverage: Global; released 2024-12-17, valid until late 2029
why_useful: Correct compass headings and model Earth's magnetic field as a reference for magnetometer-based navigation.
notes: Standard model for navigation, attitude and heading systems.

name: Canada aeromagnetic survey data compilation
publisher: Natural Resources Canada - Geological Survey of Canada
format: ZIP grids (residual total field, first vertical derivative); WMS
coverage: Canada at 200 m and 1 km resolution
why_useful: Use magnetic anomaly maps as a GPS-free navigation reference by matching magnetometer readings to the map.
notes: Files served from the Geoscience Data Repository (gdr.agg.nrcan.gc.ca).

name: OpenCelliD cell tower database
format: CSV exports (by country, worldwide, daily changes); API
coverage: 55M+ cells in 200+ countries; GSM, CDMA, UMTS, LTE, 5G NR; exports cover the last 18 months
why_useful: Estimate position from cellular signals as a backup when GNSS is jammed.
notes: SHARE-ALIKE: derived data must stay CC BY-SA 4.0 with visible credit. Free account and API token needed for downloads.

name: ISED Spectrum Management System authorization data extract
publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
format: CSV in ZIP with PDF specifications; monthly
coverage: Canada; authorized radio systems for aeronautical, broadcast, fixed, land mobile, maritime and satellite earth station services
why_useful: Map known transmitters to use broadcast towers as navigation signals of opportunity or to spot unexpected emitters.
notes: More extracts (site data, 6 GHz, TV white space) at ised-isde.canada.ca/site/spectrum-management-system/en/spectrum-management-system-data/download-sms-data

name: CelesTrak GP element sets (GNSS and LEO constellations)
licence: No licence stated; free under the CelesTrak usage policy
format: TLE/3LE, OMM XML and KVN, JSON, CSV
coverage: GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou, Starlink, Iridium NEXT, OneWeb and other groups
why_useful: Predict where GNSS and LEO satellites are, for sky plots, visibility checks or LEO signals-of-opportunity positioning.
notes: RATE LIMITS: fetch GP data no more than once every 2 hours and stop on non-200 responses or risk an IP block.

name: CWFIS fire data services (hotspots, active fires, fire weather)
publisher: Natural Resources Canada - Canadian Forest Service
licence: Open Government Licence – Canada (per CWFIS metadata; acknowledge NRCan)
format: WMS, WFS, WCS (GeoServer); CSV, GeoJSON, KML, shapefile, GeoTIFF
coverage: Canada; satellite hotspots (last 24 h), agency-reported active fires, perimeter estimates, Fire Weather Index grids
why_useful: Feed a live wildfire map and alert tool with official Canadian fire locations and fire danger.
notes: Layers include hotspots_last24hrs, activefires_current and m3_polygons_current at cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/geoserver/. FWI grid metadata also mentions an end-user agreement. Site needs JavaScript.

name: NASA FIRMS active fire data (MODIS, VIIRS, Landsat)
licence: NASA EOSDIS data: openly available to all and free of charge
format: CSV, SHP, KML, JSON; API returning CSV by area or country
coverage: Global, near real-time (real-time for US and Canada); archive: MODIS from 2000, VIIRS from 2012, Landsat from 2022
why_useful: Detect new fires within hours and check them against communities, roads and critical sites.
notes: Free MAP_KEY by email; 5000 transactions per 10 minutes. Archive downloads need an Earthdata login or email code. Near-real-time records are later replaced by science-quality data (~5 month lag).

name: Alberta historical wildfire data: 2006 to 2025
format: CSV with PDF data dictionary
coverage: Alberta, each wildfire 2006-2025: cause, size, location, dates, weather, suppression resources, area burned
why_useful: Model where and when Alberta fires start and grow to plan detection, staging and evacuations.
notes: Same record lives on open.alberta.ca/opendata/wildfire-data (returned server errors on 2026-10-04). Fires still active on 2026-02-01 lack extinguish dates. Perimeter shapefiles 1931-2025 are listed on alberta.ca/wildfire-maps-and-data.

name: Canadian National Fire Database (CNFDB) fire perimeters
publisher: Natural Resources Canada - Canadian Forest Service
format: Shapefile; WMS
coverage: Canada, 1917-2024 (start year varies by agency)
why_useful: Train fire-spread or risk models on a century of mapped fire perimeters across Canada.
notes: Not all fires are mapped and accuracy varies. Files and metadata: cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/downloads/nfdb/fire_poly/current_version/

name: FBP Fuel Types 2024, 30 m
format: GeoTIFF; WMS
coverage: National forest fuel-type map at 30 m (inputs 2020-2024)
why_useful: Estimate how fast a fire could spread toward a town by combining fuel types with weather.
notes: Built from SCANFI, ecozones and the National Burned Area Composite; used for Fire Behaviour Prediction System calculations.

name: MSC Datamart (raw weather, water and alert data)
publisher: Environment and Climate Change Canada - Meteorological Service of Canada
licence: Environment and Climate Change Canada Data Services End-use Licence (v2.1.1)
format: GRIB2, NetCDF, GeoJSON, shapefile, CSV, XML over HTTPS; AMQP push
coverage: Canada; observations, weather model output, hydrometric data, CAP weather alerts; 30-day retention
why_useful: Pull live Canadian forecasts and official weather warnings into an emergency operations dashboard.
notes: Server: dd.weather.gc.ca. CAP alerts under dd.weather.gc.ca/today/alerts/cap/. Commercial use allowed with attribution; reproduced alerts must not be altered.

name: MSC GeoMet web services (OGC API, WMS, WCS)
publisher: Environment and Climate Change Canada - Meteorological Service of Canada
licence: Environment and Climate Change Canada Data Services End-use Licence (v2.1.1)
format: WMS, WCS, OGC API (GeoJSON), STAC
coverage: Canada; weather, climate and water layers
why_useful: Add ready-made weather, climate and water layers to a map with simple web requests instead of downloading files.
notes: Anonymous and free. OGC API at api.weather.gc.ca.

name: NAAD System public alert feeds
licence: NAAD System Terms and Conditions of Use
format: CAP-CP XML over TCP stream; GeoRSS/Atom; HTTP archive
coverage: Canada; public safety alerts from authorized government issuers
why_useful: Ingest official Canadian public alerts in real time and route them to maps, teams or devices.
notes: CUSTOM TERMS: review the NAAD System Terms and Conditions of Use before building on the feeds. Connect to streaming1 or streaming2.naad-adna.pelmorex.com on TCP port 8080 (LMD User Guide). Free registration for technical bulletins. Archive: alertsarchive.pelmorex.com

name: Real-time hydrometric data
format: CSV on MSC Datamart; OGC API Features (GeoJSON); AMQP
coverage: 2,100+ stations across Canada; water level and discharge for the last 30 days
why_useful: Watch river levels near communities and trigger flood warnings when they rise quickly.
notes: Paths: dd.weather.gc.ca/hydrometric/csv/ and api.weather.gc.ca/collections/hydrometric-realtime. Historical archive: HYDAT.

name: Alberta Flood Hazard Identification Program mapping
format: File Geodatabase (ZIP); web map application
coverage: Alberta flood studies 1983-2023: inundation maps, floodway and flood fringe for the 1:100 design flood, 1:200 and 1:500 events, ice-jam floods
why_useful: Find which buildings, roads and facilities sit in mapped flood zones to plan evacuations and protection.
notes: Also listed on open.alberta.ca. Contact: epa.flood@gov.ab.ca

name: Canadian Disaster Database
format: XLSX extract (2022, English and French); online search with KML and GeoRSS export
coverage: 1,000+ disasters affecting Canadians since 1900: natural, technological and conflict events
why_useful: Analyse past disasters by type, place and cost to choose which scenarios a resilience tool should handle first.
notes: Publisher warns against simple comparisons across jurisdictions and calls recent costs preliminary. Search tool: publicsafety.gc.ca/cnt/rsrcs/cndn-dsstr-dtbs/

name: National Road Network (NRN)
format: GeoPackage, shapefile; WMS and ESRI REST
coverage: 13 provincial and territorial datasets: road and ferry segments, junctions, address ranges, road class, lanes
why_useful: Route responders and evacuees on an official national road network and test detours around closed roads.
notes: Updated annually; record last modified 2024-12-18.

name: OpenStreetMap extracts for Canada (Geofabrik)
format: .osm.pbf, .gpkg.zip (most provinces), .poly, .osc.gz
coverage: Canada (6.1 GB) and each province and territory incl. Alberta; updated daily
why_useful: Get roads, buildings, hospitals and other points of interest in one file for routing and situational-awareness maps.
notes: SHARE-ALIKE: ODbL; credit OpenStreetMap contributors. Extracts omit user names and IDs.

name: 2021 Census Profile
format: CSV, TAB, IVT
coverage: Canada, provinces, census divisions and subdivisions, census tracts, down to dissemination areas
why_useful: Estimate how many people live inside a fire or flood zone, and their characteristics, for evacuation and shelter planning.
notes: The full dissemination-area CSV is about 2.2 GB; smaller geography files exist. Join to the 2021 boundary files.

name: 2021 Census boundary files
format: Shapefile, GML, File Geodatabase; ESRI REST and WMS
coverage: Canada; provinces, census divisions and subdivisions, census tracts, dissemination areas and blocks, population centres
why_useful: Turn census tables into maps so teams can see which neighbourhoods a hazard affects.
notes: Cartographic files clip to the land mass; digital files include coastal water.

name: Open Database of Healthcare Facilities (ODHF)
format: CSV (zipped)
coverage: About 7,000 hospitals, ambulatory care and nursing or residential care facilities across Canada (version 1.1)
why_useful: Locate hospitals and care homes near a hazard to plan patient moves and ambulance routes.
notes: Compiled November 2019 to June 2020, so confirm current status locally.

name: Microsoft Canadian Building Footprints
format: GeoJSON in ZIP per province or territory (1 MB to 808 MB)
coverage: 11,842,186 building footprints across all provinces and territories
why_useful: Count buildings inside a fire or flood polygon to estimate exposure and set response priorities.
notes: SHARE-ALIKE: ODbL. Machine-generated from imagery (98.7% precision, 72.3% recall on evaluation), so some buildings are missing. Statistics Canada's Open Database of Buildings (OGL, about 4.4 million records) is an official alternative.

name: North American energy infrastructure (NACEI mapping data)
publisher: Natural Resources Canada (with US and Mexican energy departments)
format: ESRI REST and WMS services; XLS data dictionary
coverage: Canada, US, Mexico: power plants 100 MW+, renewable plants 1 MW+, refineries, LNG terminals, gas processing and storage, cross-border transmission lines and pipelines
why_useful: Map major power and fuel facilities to see which ones a wildfire, flood or storm could threaten.
notes: Public, high-level facility locations.

name: Open Government Portal (open.canada.ca)
licence: Open Government Licence – Canada (most records; check each dataset)
format: Varies by dataset (CSV, geospatial files, web services)
coverage: Federal datasets across departments, plus many federated provincial records
why_useful: Search one place for Canadian government data on transport, environment, infrastructure and more.
notes: OGL-Canada allows commercial use with attribution: 'Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Canada.'

name: Alberta Open Government Portal
licence: Open Government Licence – Alberta (most records; check each dataset)
format: Varies by dataset
coverage: About 2,900 Government of Alberta open datasets
why_useful: Find Alberta data on emergencies, energy, land and the economy to ground prototypes locally.
notes: Some dataset pages returned HTTP 520 errors on 2026-10-04; many records are mirrored on open.canada.ca. OGL-Alberta allows commercial use with attribution.

name: City of Edmonton Open Data Portal
licence: City of Edmonton Open Data Terms of Use (version 2.1)
format: Datasets, maps and charts with Socrata API access
coverage: City of Edmonton
why_useful: Ground a demo in the host city with municipal datasets and live APIs.
notes: Terms allow commercial use; attribution optional but encouraged. API docs at dev.socrata.com.

name: Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (Sentinel-1, -2, -3, -5P)
licence: Sentinel data: free, full and open (Legal Notice on the use of Copernicus Sentinel Data)
format: Sentinel products; Copernicus Browser; STAC, openEO and Sentinel Hub APIs
coverage: Global; Sentinel-1 radar, Sentinel-2 optical, Sentinel-3, Sentinel-5P
why_useful: Get free radar and optical satellite imagery over the Arctic or a fire zone for detection and change analysis.
notes: Browsing works without an account; downloads need free registration. Other portal content is for non-commercial use.

name: NASA Earthdata (EOSDIS) with Earthdata Login
licence: EOSDIS data openly available to all and free of charge, except where governed by international agreements
format: Varies by dataset; many APIs and tools
coverage: Global Earth observation archives from NASA data centres (DAACs)
why_useful: One free login unlocks NASA data used across themes, from fire detections to GNSS orbit products at CDDIS.
notes: Earthdata Login is the single sign-on for EOSDIS data centres, tools and services.

name: USGS EarthExplorer
licence: USGS-authored or produced data: U.S. Public Domain; some datasets require accepting an end-user licence agreement
format: Landsat scenes, aerial photos, DEMs and other products
coverage: Global satellite and aerial archives
why_useful: Download Landsat imagery for before-and-after views of fires, floods or ice.
notes: Login required to download or order scenes. Suggested credit: U.S. Geological Survey.

name: Natural Earth
format: Vector and raster map data
coverage: Global small-scale base map layers
why_useful: Drop in clean country, coastline and place layers for quick base maps.
notes: No permission needed; commercial use allowed.

name: GeoNames gazetteer
format: Gazetteer and postal code downloads; web services (free and premium)
coverage: Over 11 million placenames worldwide
why_useful: Turn place names in alerts or reports into coordinates, or label map points with nearby place names.
notes: Free downloads; credit GeoNames.

name: CanVec topographic data
format: Shapefile, File Geodatabase, KMZ, WMS
coverage: All of Canada; 60+ feature classes (transport, hydro, land, man-made, elevation, names) at several scales
why_useful: Add official rivers, lakes, transport and land features to Canadian maps, including remote northern areas.
notes: Record lists no planned updates; check feature dates.

name: Medium Resolution Digital Elevation Model (MRDEM)
format: VRT rasters (DTM, DSM, hillshade) with STAC API; WMS
coverage: All of Canada at 30 m, extending into US border watersheds
why_useful: Model terrain for radio line-of-sight, flood flow or drone flight planning.
notes: Designed for streaming rather than bulk download; built from Copernicus DEM and lidar-based HRDEM.
